props.title: What a visit looks like.
props.lede: Music in the common area, built from the decades the residents know, with requests taken as they come.

rows.text: The standards and the Great American Songbook: Autumn Leaves, All of Me, Someday My Prince Will Come, The Girl from Ipanema. The duo plays it without a singer, so the melodies carry the songs and anyone who wants to sing along can. A singer with a guitar is the version for a community that wants the words: the Beatles, Motown, the folk songs and the country songs from the years the residents were young. In December the same musicians play the season’s songs, which the Christmas jazz trio page covers.
Where the program wants the residents singing, Your Bird Can Sing is the booking: two musicians who play the Beatles and get the whole common area singing the choruses.

About the level of a conversation, so a resident at the back of the space hears the melody and a resident at the front can still talk to the person beside them. The musicians set it to the space, and in a small lounge the guitar plays with no amplification at all.

The same musicians play a shorter, quieter set to a smaller group, closer to the residents, leaning on the songs most likely to be recognized: the standards, a hymn or two, and the songs of the fifties and sixties. The musician follows the residents’ lead on requests and on when a set should end.

props.title: The duo, the singer, the solo, and the piano.

props.html: The jazz duo is the booking we recommend first for a common area: two instruments playing the standards, a volume two musicians can’t push past by accident, and a sound you can tell is live from across the space. It’s the size for a dining hall of sixty and for a lounge of fifteen.
The singer and guitarist is the version for a community that wants the words sung: the Beatles, Motown, the folk songs and the country songs, with the standards mixed in.

A solo guitarist plays the standards and Spanish-tinged sets instrumentally for a smaller group or a memory care neighborhood. Where the community has a piano in the common area, a pianist plays the standards and the covers on it, with a voice when the program wants singing.
The published song list is searchable on the repertoire page, and if there's a song the residents ask for, let us know and we can usually learn it.

props.title: One visit, or a standing afternoon.

props.html: Tell us the afternoon you have in mind, how often you’d like a visit and the budget line you have for live music, and we’ll come back with a recommendation and a price for that run of dates. A single visit, for a resident’s milestone birthday, a Mother’s Day tea, a summer barbecue in the courtyard or a holiday open house for families, is the same booking for one date, and a family evening that grows into a party is on private parties.
Stage sizes and power for every size are on the technical page, written so a facilities manager can check it line by line.

items.q: Do you play at assisted living and memory care communities?
items.a: Yes. A solo musician or a duo plays the common area, the dining hall or the activity space of an assisted living, memory care or independent living community, and senior centers too, usually on a weekday afternoon. Signet Artists books them across Denver and the Front Range.

No. It's a live performance for the residents, and a board-certified music therapist is a different booking with a clinical purpose. What we bring is musicians playing the songs the residents know, in the common area with no stage.

items.q: Can we book a standing monthly date?
items.a: Yes. The same weekday afternoon each month or every other week runs on one contract with one personal contact for the whole run, and the set changes from visit to visit, so the residents hear new songs beside the ones they ask for again.

items.q: How long is a visit, and what does the space need?
items.a: One set of 45 to 60 minutes, or two shorter sets with a break. A duo sets up in about 8 by 6 feet and a solo in 6 by 4, on the floor, with one outlet. Setup is 45 minutes to an hour before the program, packing up takes half an hour, and the musicians use whichever door the community prefers.

items.q: Do you provide a certificate of insurance and a W-9?
items.a: Yes, we can, and we can name the community as additional insured. Just let us know what the business office needs.
